first_ab.decision_rule_fixed_before_the_run:
Lazy contact-policy evidence A/B decision rule. Written 2026-10-11 ~12:05Z, before any build or run.

Arms (release builds, same host, one invocation):
  base = main 1a787eda
  lazy = 1a787eda + lazy_contact_evidence.patch
The patch gathers evidence cheapest first (approved, recent, thread participants, shared reservations),
only for recipients whose policy needs it, and stops once none waits. Decisions are unchanged.

Runs: paced_swarm.py, 60 agents, 300 s.
  - Order base lazy lazy base at period 6 s (~10 sends/s; normal load, where the policy step was 62 ms of a
    136 ms send).
  - Then the same order at period 2 s (saturating).

WIN (lands) only if all of the following hold:
  W1. Period 6 s, both rounds: send_message p50 and p90 are each at least 10% lower than base's.
  W2. Period 6 s, both rounds: send p99 is no more than 20% above base's, and send/fetch error counts are no
      more than base's + 3.
  W3. Period 2 s, both rounds: send p50/p90/p99 are each no more than 20% above base's (no regression at
      saturation).
  W4. Correctness:
      - tools lib, tools it (including the new shared-reservation test) and conformance pass;
      - tools clippy is clean.
      The new test passes on base too, since the eager code also computes reservation evidence. It guards
      the lazy chain: an implementation that stopped before the last source, or applied reservation
      evidence to contacts_only, fails it.

If W1 fails: report a measured null or loss (the policy step was not the cost, or the approved lookup is the
expensive one). Do not land.

Reported alongside: per-step send timings are not available in these builds (no instrumentation), so only
client latencies, errors and WAL size are reported.
first_ab.outcome: W1/W2 FAILED as written on round 1: p50 -21%/-23% both rounds, but whole-run p90 +25% and p99 +22% in round 1 (round 2: p90 -19%, p99 -67%). W3 held at period 2 s: p50 -21%/-36%, p90 -27%/-36%, p99 +5%/+11%.

replication.decision_rule_fixed_before_the_run:
Lazy contact evidence: powered replication rule. Written 2026-10-11 ~16:15Z, after ab_lazy's period-6 s
runs and before its period-2 s runs finished. It does not replace lazy_rule.txt. That run stays recorded as
FAILED W1/W2: round 1 p90 was +25% and p99 +22%; round 2 p90 was -19% and p99 -67%.

Why replicate: in ab_lazy, single runs of the identical binary differ by 36-61% in whole-run send p90/p99
(base p99 3.11 vs 4.22 s; lazy p90 0.53 vs 0.33 s; lazy p99 3.80 vs 1.38 s). The first-minute warm-up drives
this: every first contact runs the full evidence chain plus an auto-handshake in both arms. With 2 runs per
arm, a +/-10-20% tail threshold cannot be decided. The thresholds stay the same; only the sample grows.

Runs (only if ab_lazy's period-2 s check, W3, holds): the same build16 binaries, paced_swarm.py, 60 agents,
period 6 s, 300 s.
  Order: base lazy lazy base base lazy lazy base base base. That is 5 runs per arm, plus an A/A pair at the
  end (runs 9-10, both base).

Decision (pooled over the 5 runs per arm, every send of every run):
  P1. Pooled lazy send p50 and p90 are each at least 10% lower than pooled base's.
  P2. Pooled lazy send p99 is no more than 20% above pooled base's. Error count is no more than base's + 3.
  P3. Per-run consistency: lazy's median per-run p50 is lower than base's median per-run p50.
  P4. A/A sanity: base run 9 vs run 10 pooled p50 differ by less than 10%. If not, the host is too noisy and
      the replication is void (report it, no verdict).
  WIN if P1-P3 hold and P4 is valid. Then the change lands, with both results (the failed 2x2 and this
  replication) in the commit and on the bead.
  Otherwise LOSS or NULL: not landed, reported.
replication.outcome: WIN: P1, P2, P3 hold and the A/A pair is valid (see lazy_pooled.py output).
